newsitem.title: USA: Int'l Cutlery seeks Nasdaq hearing.
newsitem.headline: Int'l Cutlery seeks Nasdaq hearing.

text.p: International Cutlery Ltd, which faces possible Nasdaq delisting for noncompliance with listing requirements, said Friday it was seeking a hearing to explain its side.
Joel Silver, president, said that the Nasdaq panel hearing could take place "sometime in July."
Silver said that, as a stock quoted on Nasdaq's SmallCap Market, International Cutlery is required to have at least two market makers and that its stock price should trade at least $1.
"My records show we have more than two market makers," he said.
"I can't argue about the price," he said. At midday, the stock traded at about $0.09.
He said, however, that at the hearing, "we can show them (Nasdaq) how we can improve that."
The company said it had been notified by the Nasdaq that its common stock and Class A and B warrants did not meet listing criteria and faced delisting.
It said it understood that pending the Nasdaq panel's determination, its comon stock and warrants will remain listed on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market.
